A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RRPO self-alignment work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite added appendix material and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of RRPO on three video-language models, including benchmark comparisons, ablations and detailed appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds statistical comparisons and qualitative success and failure cases.

M1.justification: Sections 2–3 and Appendix A retain the same preference-data construction, concept-level rewards, token-wise KL regularization, loss and pseudocode. Sequence-length notation edits do not change the method.

E1.justification: The VideoChat-IT training sources and eight evaluation benchmarks remain unchanged. Added qualitative examples concern the existing temporal reasoning, hallucination, captioning and short/long video-understanding tasks.

E2.justification: Figure S4 adds a DPO response to the LongVU elevator-transition example that v1 Figure 1 compared only between the base model and RRPO. The main quantitative comparator sets, including DPO, DPA, TDPO, DDPO and TPO, remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported model configurations, training budgets, benchmark metrics, data-size sweeps, frame counts and subtitle settings are retained. The added significance analysis does not establish a change to the underlying evaluation design.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds illustrative comparative case studies, including persistent description hallucinations in Figure S8 and long-video failures in Figure S9. Existing component, perturbation, data-size, frame-count and subtitle analyses remain unchanged; the additions do not constitute a new systematic robustness evaluation.

E5.justification: v1 provides point estimates without a statistical significance procedure. v2 Appendix C introduces an SE-based 95% significance criterion and marks significant RRPO comparisons across the existing benchmark suite in Table S1. No repeated-run counts or seed information are introduced.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–8 and the detailed results renumbered from S1–S4 to S2–S5 are unchanged. New Table S1 reports significance findings and some conflicting scores: TPO's MLVU result is 68.9, versus 68.7 in the retained Table 3. Appendix G also adds qualitative outcomes, including failures; these additions do not establish improved headline performance.

T1.justification: Appendix C newly defines SE = sqrt(Score1 × (1 − Score2) / n) and Adjusted Delta = Delta − 1.96 × SE as its significance rule. The RRPO loss definitions, gradient reasoning and Appendix B derivations otherwise remain unchanged apart from equivalent notation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning self-alignment, refined rewards, regularization, training stability and improved video understanding. The new appendix evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Figures S8–S9 newly discuss persistent hallucinations and attribute remaining long-video failures to base-model architectural constraints and limited training compute. Appendix F also proposes applicability to language and multimodal generative models. Earlier mechanism explanations remain intact.

D1.justification: The new Appendix D introduction names GPT4o, while Section 4 still specifies GPT-4o-mini, creating a documentation ambiguity rather than establishing changed processing. The checklist adds review-period anonymous-sharing statements. Prompts, pseudocode, hyperparameters, hardware, training-time disclosures and public resource links are retained.

R1.justification: The same 85 references and substantive positioning against prior alignment methods are retained. Bibliographic back-reference changes and expanded comparison headings do not introduce new related work.

P1.justification: The original narrative and section order are largely unchanged. v2 adds appendix subsections, broader-impact and qualitative-results sections, and a conference checklist, alongside localized wording, notation, heading and publication-footnote edits.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual evidence with significance-marked Table S1 and six qualitative figures, S4–S9. Existing prompt boxes are reformatted and captioned as Figures S2–S3, while detailed-results and hyperparameter tables are relocated and renumbered. Main figures and tables remain largely unchanged.

improvement.justification: The added failure cases and explicit limitations improve transparency. However, Appendix C does not justify its cross-model SE formula as uncertainty for a difference in scores, undermining its claimed 95% significance judgments, and Table S1 conflicts with retained numerical results. With the core method and benchmark evidence unchanged, these benefits and reliability problems leave the net quality direction uncertain.
